$comment: The source of sf-settings' element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js), in the 1.4 form (scripts/generate-component-files.mjs writes rule.js, aliases.json, studio.fixture.json, studio.scenario.json, probe.json and smart.manifest.json from it). A new component, made against standard simai.smart-component 1.3.14 and vocabulary 1.1.5: compact settings of the owner decision of 2026-11-06 (Federation bus msg-cbe15ae81eab468fbbe8), composed over sf-menu-context.

items.summary: The settings, each holding its own value: {id, type: switch, text, value: true}, {id, type: choice, text, value: <option id>, options: [{id, text, icon?}]}, {id, type: range, text, value, min, max, step, unit}, {id, type: color, text, value: <palette hue name or #rrggbb>, options?: [hue names], custom?: false} (C85: the current colour as the row's circle, a level of hue circles and «Свой цвет…», which opens sf-input-color's window on «Своё»; ten hues by default), {type: heading, text}, {type: separator}, {type: group, text, items}; icon and caption on a setting, disabled on a setting or an option, tile: true on a switch the tiles look puts on top. A property, or the JSON island a server prints; in the panel look also {id, type: fields, text, options: [{id, text, checked, pinned, disabled}], sortable, pinnable}: a list of many to check (a table's columns), ordered by a handle and Alt+arrows when sortable, pinned on top when pinnable; its value is [{id, checked, pinned}] in order, the pinned first

look.summary: The arrangement. drill: the current value under the name and a chevron, the options open in the same panel with a way back. rows: the name at the start, the control at the end -- quiet pills, a switch, a slider. tiles: the switches used most as tiles on top (those marked tile, else the top level's), the rest as rows. panel (owner decision C106): a list's view settings in a panel of its own -- the groups as sections in one scroll, or as tabs when the panel has a search and a group holds a fields list; a checked field is the theme's light fill with a check at the inline end, a choice of one the fill alone; a dialog over the page, a bottom sheet on a phone

apply.summary: How the panel look applies a change (C106 (4)). instant: at once, as every look -- change, then changed; the footer holds one «Сбросить» (the declared values back). button: a filter's -- the changes wait in the panel until «Применить (N)» (N: the checked fields and the switches on), then go out as change and changed and the popup closes; «Сбросить» puts the declared values into the panel, and closing drops what was not applied. The other looks apply at once

search.summary: A search over the panel look's rows (C106 (7), C30 R071: a setting, never by the number of rows; the docs advise it from ten rows): a header over the body; the rows are filtered as the field is typed in -- no case, ё as е, on a row's text, caption and keywords. With it, a group that holds a fields list makes the groups tabs. Down from the field enters the rows

size.summary: The menu's rung: rows of 32 px at 1/2, of 40 px at 1

for.summary: The id of a page element, or several separated by spaces, that opens the panel when pressed; the trigger slot is the other way. With neither the panel stands open in the page's flow

remember.summary: A name to keep the values under: they are a preference of the person (SF.Preferences key sf-settings/<name>; in the browser localStorage sf-pref:sf-settings/<name>, and a host that keeps preferences for its user gets them), written after every change and put back into the items before the first drawing

label.summary: The panel's accessible name. «Настройки» / «Settings» in the page language when not set

values.summary: Every setting's value by its id: {theme: 'dark', sound: true, scale: 110}. Read-only; the values live in the items

value.summary: The value asked for: a boolean for a switch, a number for a range, the option's id for a choice.

item.summary: The item with the value asked for.

change.summary: A person asks to change a setting: the request, sent before the value is written. Cancelled, nothing changes and the row keeps the value it had until the page answers with setValue

item.summary: The item, with its new value.

changed.summary: The fact: the value is written into its item, the row shows it and remember has kept it. The page applies the setting here. reset raises it once for each setting it moved; setValue and setAll raise nothing

reset.summary: The declared values are asked back (the reset action): the request. Cancelled, the current values stay

open.summary: A popup panel of look="panel" asks to open (its trigger, show): the request, sent before it is drawn. Cancelled, it stays closed. The other looks open their inner sf-menu-context, which sends its own open

opened.summary: The popup panel of look="panel" is open and drawn

close.summary: The popup panel of look="panel" asks to close: escape, outside (a press outside), close (the close button, the trigger again) or api (Apply, Tab out, a script); unsaved says a draft of apply="button" moved something. Cancelled, it stays open

closed.summary: The popup panel of look="panel" is closed

set-value.summary: Writes one setting's value into its item: the page's answer to a cancelled change, or a value restored on load. Raises nothing. Refused with not-found when no item carries the id, with invalid when the item cannot hold the value

x-returns.description: {outcome}: applied; refused with not-found or invalid.

set-all.summary: Writes a map of values -- {id: value} -- into the items that carry those ids: a panel restored from storage in one call. Raises nothing. Refused with not-found when no id of the map is an item's

x-returns.description: {outcome, count}: how many items were written.

show.summary: Goes straight to one setting: a popup opens against its trigger, the drill look opens the levels down to it, and the focus goes to its row. Refused with not-found when no item carries the id; unavailable with no-trigger for a popup whose trigger is not in the page; cancelled when the menu's open was cancelled

reset.summary: Puts the declared values back -- the values the items carried when the page gave them -- after asking reset; changed goes out once for each setting that moved. A listener that cancels reset keeps the current values

x-returns.description: {outcome, count}: applied with how many settings moved, or cancelled.

relations.name: cl-button
$comment: The panel look's footer and the close button: fetched after the page is ready, not held up front for every menu look.

relations.name: cl-tabs
$comment: The panel look's groups as tabs.

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16): the build does not compile template.html yet, so a second copy of the markup would only drift from the one that draws.

accessibility.$comment: The panel is sf-menu-context named by label (role menu): a switch is a menuitemcheckbox, a choice's options menuitemradio, a range the platform's slider, a drilling choice a menuitem that opens its level. One tab stop, the arrows move, Enter and Space change, Right and Left go in and out of a level, Escape goes back a level and then closes a popup with the focus back on the trigger. The trigger the page gives gets aria-haspopup menu and aria-expanded. The panel look (C106, DP-7) is not a menu: a popup is a dialog named by label (a group in the page's flow) with its own closing -- the close button, Escape, a press outside, Tab out of it (a phone's sheet keeps Tab inside). Each list is one Tab stop (DP-4): the arrows walk its rows (a radio group chooses as it moves), Home and End go to its ends, Space and Enter check a field or turn a switch; a field is a checkbox, a choice's option a radio, a switch a switch. In a list that orders, Alt+Up and Alt+Down move the row within its block and a live region says its place («Срок: 3 из 8»); the inline-end arrow reaches the row's pin, a toggle button.

x-summary: Compact settings: a few settings a person changes on the spot, as data, each holding its own value, drawn by sf-menu-context in one of three looks -- drill (the value under the name, the options in the same panel), rows (the control at the row's end) or tiles (the switches used most as tiles on top). With a trigger it opens over the page; without one it stands in the page's flow. A change is asked first (cancellable), then written and reported; remember keeps the values for the person. The panel look (C106) draws a panel of its own for a list's view settings: sections or tabs, fields lists with a check, a handle, a pin and a search, applied at once or by «Применить».

x-source.brief: Owner decision 2026-11-06 relayed by the docs thread (Federation bus msg-cbe15ae81eab468fbbe8): compact settings get their own public Smart component again, sf-settings, composed over sf-menu-context the way sf-language composes its parts; not sf-settings-menu (removed 2026-10-30, not revived) and no second menu engine; items as data (property and island) of kinds switch, choice, range, heading, separator, group with the value in the item; look=drill|rows|tiles after the recipes of ui-doc 04d391db (examples/smart-components/context-menu/settings-{drill,rows,tiles}); popup with a trigger slot or for, or inline; change (cancellable, before the write), changed, reset (cancellable); setValue, setAll, show, reset with the menu's outcomes; 280 px panel, names wrap, values ellipsis with a tooltip; size 1/2 and 1; optional remember via SF.Preferences; no CSS variables of its own

x-decisions: name: sf-settings, the family settings (owner, 2026-11-06). sf-settings-menu stays removed: it was folded into sf-context-menu on 2026-10-30 without an alias, and no alias brings it back.

reuse: the element draws nothing itself and has no sheet. The panel is sf-menu-context with the items as its entries -- the value rows (switch, choice, range), headings, separators, groups and tiles are the menu's, and so are their keys and roles. Mixed menus (a profile menu with a theme choice) keep the value rows of sf-menu-context directly.

items: the menu's vocabulary (id, type, text, caption, icon, options of {id, text, icon}, min, max, step, unit, items, disabled) with two differences: a choice holds its value as value -- the chosen option's id -- rather than as checked marks (options[].checked is still read when value is missing), and a group shows its text as a heading over its rows.

looks: one attribute after today's recipes. drill = the menu's submenu=drill with every choice view=drill (the value under the name, a chevron, the options in place with a check mark and a way back); rows = no levels, choices as quiet pills at the row's end, switches, sliders; tiles = a group view=tiles on top with the switches marked tile: true (else the top level's switches), a separator, the rest as rows.

popup or inline: the trigger slot (the children without a slot, as sf-search) or for=<id> make it a popup -- the menu's openFor against the trigger's own control, the top layer, Escape and a press outside close it, the focus goes back. With neither it is inline, always open in the page's flow.

values: the value lives in the item and nowhere else; values is the map read from the items. A person's change goes out as change (cancellable, the menu's request forwarded) before anything is written; not cancelled, the value is written into the item, remember keeps it, and changed is the fact. setValue and setAll write without events, as the menu's; reset asks reset and then reports changed once for each setting that moved. The menu's own select, change, changed and reset stay inside.

width: the panel is 280 px in every look -- the drilling menu's own width (--sf-context-menu-inline-size, f7 + a8), given to the menu as its lower and upper bound -- so a long name wraps and a long value ends in an ellipsis with the whole of it in title.
geometry: the menu's two rungs, size 1/2 (32 px rows) and 1 (40 px); every sub-element is the menu's own, on the ladder.

remember: SF.Preferences key sf-settings/<name>, the whole value map, written after every change, setValue, setAll and reset, and put back into the items the first time the element meets them, before its first drawing (no flash of the declared values). The declared values stay the page's for reset.

css-variables: none of its own. The menu looks have no sheet (sf-menu-context's public variables reach them, --sf-context-menu-inline-size sets their width); the panel look's sheet has only internal variables (--sf-settings-panel--*).

version 1.0.1 (2026-11-07): the drill look's option level marks the chosen option by the soft fill of a chosen row, not a check mark (sf-menu-context 1.7.0, owner decision R016; rule 1 applied to the drill look: it reads as the language list does, and the options use the whole width); a search in the panel keeps its field and scrolls the rows under it. Settings, values and events unchanged; docs and first-paint snapshots follow.

version 1.0.2 (2026-11-08): a patch, nothing drawn differently by this element. Its first-paint sheet list names the kbd sheet (component.kbd 1.1.0, docs review R030): sf-button 1.8.0 draws a shortcut's keys with it, and every component that draws an sf-button asks for it before the first paint. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.0.3 (2026-11-08): a patch, nothing drawn differently by this element. Its first-paint snapshots follow the actions block (docs review R031, R032; decisions C13-C15): the sf-button and sf-button-icon it draws ask for the screen-reader-only utility sheet (sf-button 1.9.0, sf-button-icon 1.7.0), an sf-button-close it draws asks for its own sheet (C14), and sf-input's classes follow its outer sizes (sf-input 1.6.0). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.0.4 (2026-11-09): a patch, nothing drawn or done differently. The generated reference gives each action's method its one object argument, setValue({id, value}), setAll({values}), show({id}), where it read the parameters one by one (standard §4.4: the parameters arrive as one object); the element's code also takes the value alone, show(<string>), and the reference says so (x-registry.action-calls). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.0.5 (2026-11-09): a patch, nothing drawn or done differently. show reads sf-menu-context's openFor answer as an outcome (sf-menu-context 1.12.2) and still as the boolean an earlier menu gave. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.0.6 (2026-11-10, folded into 1.1.0 in the same pair, never released alone): a patch; nothing in the component changed. Its panels are sf-menu-context, which since 1.14.1 draws the context-menu frame without the late utility classes, so the first-paint snapshots follow; the component takes a patch with them. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.1.0 (2026-11-10, owner decision C32, addendum 2026-11-09): the panel's default width is the menu's ceiling of the popup widths, core's --sf-popup-menu-max-width: 18rem (288 px), 16rem (256 px) in compact density. It was 280 px at every density (f7 + a8). --sf-context-menu-inline-size still sets it. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.2.0 (2026-11-12, owner decision C85, prototype theme-generator-study #practice-menu): a minor. A new item type color: a colour setting beside the theme, as compact as «Настройки чтения». Its row leads with the current colour as a circle (sf-menu-context 1.15.0 swatch), the value under the name in the drill look; it opens a level of palette hues, each a circle and its word -- options (hue names, or {id, text}) or the ten of the accepted menu: red, orange, amber, green, teal, sky, blue, violet, pink, gray -- and, unless custom is false, «Свой цвет…», which closes the menu and opens sf-input-color's window on «Своё» against the trigger (palette="false": the level is the palette). The value is what sf-input-color stores (C83): a hue by its name, the same in every language, or an own colour's code #rrggbb; a hue it does not offer or a code with custom false is refused. A colour chosen in the window is asked (change) and written (changed) as a row's value is. The window's holder is inert while closed. Words: the hue names, own-color, own-color-value. Settings, events and the other types unchanged.

version 1.2.0, also (2026-11-12, owner decision C106, R193; defects DP-1..DP-9 of the dropdown-panels study): a fourth look, panel -- a list's view settings in a panel of this element's own rather than a mode of the action menu: the groups as sections in one scroll by default, as tabs when the panel has a search and a group holds a fields list (more than three groups belong in sf-drawer, the docs say); a new item type fields -- the one row data API for a list of many to check, order and pin, so a product stops drawing its own rows (sf-table-column-option, sf-table-settings-row); a checked field is the theme's light fill (--sf-primary-container) with a check at the inline end, the handle at the row's start, a choice of one the fill alone, a switch row its switch; the hover plate and the inset of C05, the H4 text inset of C77/C105, the popup panel's step of the widths of C32 (--sf-popup-panel-width); one Tab stop per list with the arrows inside, Alt+arrows with a live announcement, a drag by the handle; apply instant (one «Сбросить») or button (a filter: «Сбросить» and «Применить (N)»); search; a sheet at the bottom on a phone. The scroll area follows the inset rule (I on every side; a scrollbar that takes room is I + thumb + I = 14, and the body drops its inline-end padding; no scrollbar-gutter). It has a sheet of its own now (scss/_smart__settings.scss) and the panel's words in lang. The drill, rows and tiles looks are unchanged; view, the name C106 used for the look, is reserved by standard §3.1 (and refused by the runtime), so the panel is a value of look, the setting C106 calls «вид».

version 1.2.0 also carries (2026-11-12, C106 follow-up 6): the popup panel of look="panel" sends sf-menu-context's open/close events under its own tag, with the same names and details: sf-settings-open (cancelable, no detail) before it is drawn, sf-settings-opened when drawn, sf-settings-close (cancelable, {reason: close|escape|outside|api, unsaved}) and sf-settings-closed ({reason}). unsaved is true when a draft of apply="button" holds a value the items do not. A prevented open keeps it closed (show() answers cancelled); a prevented close keeps it open; leaving the page closes without asking. The other looks keep the inner sf-menu-context's events.

version 1.2.0, also (written on the branch as 1.1.1; 2026-11-13, defect BT-2, rules C15 / CB-01): a patch, nothing drawn differently. The popup example, the probe and the docs give the trigger sf-button-icon appearance="ghost", the name of the no-fill look, where they wrote link, its former name (an alias until 2027-01-01). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

forbidden_client_responsibilities: applying what a setting means (a dark theme, a dense table): the page listens to changed
saving the values on a server (cancel change, save, answer with setValue)
a menu of actions or a mixed menu (sf-menu-context with its value rows)

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-settings for a small set of settings a person changes on the spot -- a reader's theme and text size, a table's view, a chat's sound -- opened from a button or standing in a panel.
do_not: Do not use sf-settings for a menu of actions or a mixed menu; use sf-menu-context with its value rows
Do not use sf-settings-menu; it was removed and is not an alias
Do not keep a setting's value outside its item; read values or listen to changed
Do not use sf-settings for a long form with validation; use a form

keyboard: Tab reaches the panel's one tab stop; the arrows move between rows, Home and End go to the ends
Enter or Space turns a switch, chooses an option or opens a drilling choice; Right goes in, Left and Escape go back
A slider takes the side arrows; Escape on the top level closes a popup and returns focus to the trigger
accessibility.focus: A popup takes the focus on its first row and gives it back to the trigger when it closes; inline the focus stays where the person is.
